title: Halifax 1917: The Floating Arsenal That Exploded in Harbour
summary: Covers how, on the morning of the sixth of December, nineteen seventeen, the French munitions ship Mont-Blanc collided with the Norwegian ship Imo in the Narrows of Halifax harbour, caught fire, and exploded about twenty minutes later in the largest man-made blast before the atomic bomb. The episode follows the destruction of the Richmond district, about two thousand dead and nine thousand injured, the telegraph warning sent by train dispatcher Vince Coleman, the blizzard that struck the next day, and the Christmas tree Halifax still sends to Boston every year in thanks for its help.
